title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents
gist: SELFCOMPACT lets an LLM agent decide when to summarize its own context, using a compaction tool plus a lightweight rubric of when to fire or suppress, with no fine-tuning. Across six benchmarks and seven models it matches or beats fixed-interval summarization at 30-70% lower per-question cost.

themes.theme: Context rot in long agent traces

insights.claim: Long agent traces of chains of thought and tool calls accumulate stale content that anchors later generations and eventually outgrows the context window.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Context management is a core bottleneck for long-horizon agents and drives token cost.
insights.locator: Long agent traces composed of chains of thought

insights.claim: Existing scaffolds compact context at fixed intervals triggered by a token threshold, which ignores trajectory structure and risks discarding partial results mid-derivation or mid-search.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Naive compaction can degrade agent accuracy; smarter triggers are a differentiator.
insights.locator: Such triggers pay no heed to trajectory structure

insights.claim: SELFCOMPACT lets the model itself decide when and how to compact by pairing a compaction tool for summarizing context with a lightweight rubric on when to fire (sub-task resolved, trajectory converging) and when to suppress (mid-derivation, or stuck).
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A prompt-level scaffold improves agents without training, so gains are available to any model user.

insights.claim: Both elements are required: the tool alone is used unevenly by open-weight models, often at unhelpful moments or not at all, while the rubric alone cannot act.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Tool availability does not equal competent use; scaffolding quality matters for open-weight agents.

insights.claim: The approach elicits effective adaptive compaction without any fine-tuning or external supervision.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Zero training cost lowers the barrier to adoption in agent products.
insights.locator: Together, they elicit effective adaptive compaction

insights.claim: Tested on six benchmarks (competitive math and agentic search) and seven models, SELFCOMPACT matches or exceeds fixed-interval summarization at a fraction of the token cost.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Better accuracy per token directly improves agent unit economics.
insights.locator: We present empirical results on six benchmarks

insights.claim: Versus a no-summarization baseline, SELFCOMPACT improves by up to 18.1 points on math and 5-9 points on agentic search, at 30-70% lower per-question cost.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Cost reductions of 30-70% per question could reduce inference spend for long-running agents.
insights.locator: improving over a no-summarization baseline by up to 18.1 points

insights.claim: Unprompted models cannot reliably tell when their own context is rotting, a meta-cognitive gap that a lightweight rubric closes, so when to compact is a capability scaffolds can supply without training.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Value may accrue to scaffolding and orchestration layers rather than only to model training.
insights.locator: Our results expose a meta-cognitive gap

insights.claim: Related Apple work on training one LLM agent jointly across diverse interactive environments notes that existing curriculum and data-selection strategies allocate training at the environment level or use local reward signals, ignoring relationships between rollouts across environments.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Generalist-agent training recipes are still immature.
insights.locator: Training a single LLM agent jointly across diverse

insights.claim: Related Apple work proposes a rubric-based reward framework for open-domain question answering, generating query-specific rubrics grounded in retrieved evidence and split into multiple quality dimensions.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Rubrics are recurring as both reward and inference-time control mechanisms.
insights.locator: We introduce a rubric-based reward framework
